title: Friction as one of the forces
canonical_question: How does friction fit into the net force on a sliding object?
summary: Friction is a contact force that acts along a surface, always opposing the relative sliding.
If your push exceeds friction, the net force is forward and the crate accelerates; if friction wins, it slows or stays put.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: A force that opposes sliding
sections.body_md: Friction is a contact force that acts along a surface, always opposing the relative sliding. When you push a crate, friction points backward against your push. It is one of the forces you add up to find the net force.

sections.heading: Its effect on motion
sections.body_md: If your push exceeds friction, the net force is forward and the crate accelerates; if friction wins, it slows or stays put. Reduce friction, as on ice, and a small push produces a large net force. Friction rarely acts alone but always counts in the sum.

key_points: It enters the net force like any force.
Its balance with the push sets the motion.
core.bridge_to_parent: It adds friction to the objective’s catalogue of forces.
